newsitem.title: UK: British lottery firm hunts for $3.5 million winner.
newsitem.headline: British lottery firm hunts for $3.5 million winner.

text.p: The organisers of Britain's national lottery said on Saturday they were trying to find an 89-year-old woman who says she has a winning ticket worth 2.1 million pounds ($3.5 million).
The woman wrote to her local newspaper in eastern England, the Hull Daily Mail, saying her late husband bought the ticket in May but died before he could collect his winnings.
She said she did not want to identify herself as the resulting publicity would be the death of her. But she wanted the money to go to the hospitals which looked after her husband when he was ill.
"It was a grand feeling to win, but too late....What would be the point of the money? I have no family or friends, just a helper," she wrote.
Camelot, the firm which runs the weekly lottery draw, said it would be unable to hand over the cash unless the pensioner was found by a deadline for winning claims next Thursday.
Camelot spokeswoman Taryn Hilburn said the firm would ensure the woman's identity would not be made public if she came forward.
"If she wanted to give all the money away, they could even help her do that," said Hilburn.
"She would have to accept the money from us first. We can't give it away on her behalf."
